newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer as heady gains continue.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer as heady gains continue.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer Thursday in good volume, the market steadily moving higher to set the third life-of-contract high in a week with prices now at their best in almost a year.
But copper was looking overbought and ripe for a correction, some dealers said, while others did not expect any further major gains in the absence of unforseen glitches.

"I am not, from these price levels, real bullish," David Rinehimer of Smith Barney said. "Fundamentally it's hard to see, in my opinion, prices going much above 120.00 cents without buying from China or disruption in supplies."
July COMEX copper hit a new life-of-contract hight midsession at 119.70 cents per pound, before easing back to close at 118.95 cents, up 0.75 cent.
July was able to close above the previous life-of-contract high of 118.85 cents, floor sources noted.
Spot May settled 0.75 cent firmer at 119.30 cents after a brief foray to a high of 120.20 cents.
LME stocks continue to fall, off 975 tonnes Thursday at 139,000 tonnes, with some traders saying inventory must continue to dwindle to support prices are their current high levels.
